author: Madison Magazine Staff
title: Top things to do this month in Madison - NewsBreak
text:
By Madison Magazine Staff ,
16 hours ago “The Great Gatsby” A Broadway hit now on its first North American tour, this musical adaptation of F. Scott Fitzgerald's Roaring Twenties tale features a jazz- and pop-infused score, lavish choreography, and plenty of spectacle. Through A ug. 2 at Overture Hall, Overture Center for the Arts, 201 State St.
Andrew Dismukes Fresh off another season on "Saturday Night Live," the comic (and awesome character actor) offers dry, off-kilter storytelling and quietly absurd observations that have made him a standout on the show July 30-Aug. 1 at Comedy on State, 202 State St.
Sugar Maple Music Festival From bluegrass and Cajun to old-time string bands, this two-day festival turns Lake Farm Park into one big front porch, with national acts, workshops and jam sessions where musicians and audiences mingle. July 31 -Aug. 1 at William G. Lunney Lake Farm County Park, 4330 Libby Road
Native Art Marketplace This annual gathering fills Frank Lloyd Wright's Taliesin with Indigenous artists demonstrating everything from quillwork and black ash basketry to jewelry and painting, alongside performances and storytelling. Aug . 1-2 at Taliesin Hillside, 6604 Hwy. 23, Spring Green
Indigo Dying Workshop If you've ever wanted to try natural dyeing without investing in studio classes, this workshop offers a hands-on introduction using fresh indigo leaves and a little elbow grease. Aug. 1, 10 a.m.-noon, Allen Centennial Garden, 620 Babcock Drive
Madison Comedy Week More than 90 comedians fan out across 10 venues for a week of stand-up, improv and offbeat showcases, with highlights including Stoughton native and Second City Chicago alum Natasha Pearl Hansen, former SNL cast member Luke Null, and festival favorites like the Chicago vs. Milwaukee Roast Battle and the Madison Comedy Week All-Stars showcase. Aug. 3-8 at venues across Madison
Art on Main From handmade jewelry to paintings created on the spot, the creative outputs at this festival turn Cambridge’s downtown into a working studio where visitors can meet artists and see the process behind the finished piece. Aug. 7-8 throughout downtown Cambridge, including Art Hub, 145 W. Main St., Cambridge
NeuroArts Festival & Sound Garden The emerging field of neuroarts gets the spotlight with this festival blending art, music and science to explore how creative experiences can influence well-being. Expect an immersive Sound Garden, poetry and weaving workshops, a performance by Fresco Opera, and other events designed to engage the senses. Aug. 12-15 at Olbrich Botanical Gardens, 3330 Atwood Ave.
Eken Park Festival This bash keeps things intentionally neighborhood-sized, as a brass band, petting zoo, local vendors and great bands all share the same block. Don't miss the headliners, The Claudettes , a Chicago band with sultry jazz-pop swagger. Aug. 15, 11 a.m.-8 p.m. at Eken Park, 2407 Coolidge St.
The Earthlings The Madison band brings its mix of folk, rock and Americana to a lounge setting for a night of original music. Expect rootsy arrangements, songwriting and storytelling, with music that draws from a range of influences. Aug. 15, 8 p.m. at Garver Lounge, 3241 Garver Green
Ice Cream Boat Float Lake Wingra becomes the route to dessert during this annual event, where boaters, kayakers and paddleboarders head out to a floating ice cream barge to build their own sundaes on the water. Bring your own craft or rent one from Wingra Boats for the afternoon. Aug. 16, 3-5 p.m. at Wingra Boats, 824 Knickerbocker St.
Coffee Break Festival Stoughton leans into its claim as the birthplace of the coffee break with a festival built around the daily ritual that started there in the 1880s. Sample local brews in the Coffee Brew-Off, check out the Cup O’ Joe All Wheels Show featuring vintage vehicles, and browse arts and crafts. Aug. 15, 8 a.m.-2 p.m. at Mandt Park, 400 Mandt Parkway, Stoughton
Curd Fest Wisconsin’s favorite squeaky snack gets the star treatment during this afternoon of creative curd creations from local vendors, a cheese curd-eating contest, live music from RailHoppers and The Finding North Band, plus games and activities. Aug. 15, 3-6 p.m. at Breese Stevens Field, 917 E. Mifflin St.
Madison Night Market Downtown stays open late for the chance to discover local makers, small businesses and pop-up experiences. The market features more than 100 vendors alongside food, drinks, performances and activities worth staying out later for. Aug. 20, 5-9 p.m. on State Street and the Capitol Square
Sun Prairie Sweet Corn Festival Eighty tons of sweet corn are on the menu at this annual Sun Prairie tradition, which pairs its famous corn feed with carnival rides, live music, a parade, food vendors and family activities. The five-day festival has been celebrating the city’s favorite crop since 1953. Aug. 19-23 at Angell Park, 200 Park St., Sun Prairie
Pizza on the Farm This 'za comes with a view of where some of the ingredients begin. Go for the wood-fired pies topped with seasonal produce, plus local beer, wine and cocktails. August 27, 4:30-9 p.m. at Four Winds Farm, 5735 Adams Road, Fitchburg
Orton Park Festival The Marquette neighborhood’s annual summer gathering returns with three days of free music, food vendors, local beer and one of its most recognizable traditions: Cycropia Aerial Dance performing above Orton Park. Aug. 28-30 at Orton Park, 1103 Spaight St.
Thirsty Troll Brewfest The trolls of Mount Horeb find their natural habitat: a ski hill full of craft beer. This annual fest brings regional breweries, food, live music and outdoor activities to Tyrol Basin, with beer tastings, games, volleyball and chairlift rides rounding out the afternoon. Aug. 29, 1-5 p.m. at 3487 Bohn Road, Mount Horeb
North Star Dance Theater An evening of new ballet and contemporary dance closes out North Star Dance Theatre’s season with Dusk , featuring original works from five choreographers: Jacob Ashley, Bri Lucey, Rachelle Butler, Malachi Squires and Juan Carlos Diaz-Valez. Aug. 28-29 at MyArts Starlight Theater, 1055 E. Mifflin St.
UFA Championship Weekend The UFA’s top teams come to Madison. Four division champions battle in semifinal matchups for a spot in the title game. The hometown Madison Radicals could be part of the action if they make the cut, adding a local stake to one of ultimate frisbee’s biggest events of the year. Aug. 27, 6-10 p.m. at Breese Stevens Field, 917 E. Mifflin St.
